body.h1: IN THE UNITED STATES PATENT AND TRADEMARK OFFICE
body.p: Application of: Shimon Pertsel et al.
Serial No.: 17/873,682
Title: AUTOMATIC COLLISION DETECTION, WARNING,
body.h1: AVOIDANCE AND PREVENTION IN PARKED CARS
body.p: Filed: July 26, 2022
Attorney Docket No.: 8611.00175c Examiner: Frank T Glenn III
Art Unit: 3662
Sir:

The undersigned, Christopher P. Maiorana, Esq., hereby petitions under 37 C.F.R. §1.181 for submission of a new non-final Office Action and/or entry of an Amendment After Final, filed November 30, 2023, for the above-referenced patent application in order to remove issues for appeal under M.P.E.P. §714.13.

h1.u: R E M A R K S

body.p: The following statement of facts involved, the point(s) to be reviewed and action requested are submitted in support of the petition as required under 37 C.F.R. § 1.181(b).
The following statement of facts provide support for the point(s) to be reviewed and the action(s) requested:

The Examiner, Frank T Glenn III, issued a non-final Office Action on May 26, 2023 for U.S. Patent Application 17/873,682 rejecting and/or objecting to all of the originally filed claims 1-19. Claim 7 was objected to for an informality. Claims 1-2 and 4-19 were rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-18 of U.S. Patent No. 11,427,195 B1. A notice was provided that independent

claims 1, 11 and 19 were being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. §112(f). Claims 1, 2, 4-18 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103. Dependent claim 3 and independent claim 19 were identified as having allowable matter. In particular, claim 11 was rejected over (U.S. Patent No. 10,424,204 B1), in view of Sabeti (U.S. Application No 2015/0175072 A1), and in further view of Nagy (U.S. Application No. 2020/0132803 Al).
Applicants' representative filed an Amendment on August 23, 2023 that (i) amended claims 1, 2, 7, 8, and 11, and (ii) provided a Terminal Disclaimer.
Arguments were presented in the Amendment filed on August

23, 2023 that (i) claim 7 was amended as suggested by the Examiner to overcome the objection to claim 7, (ii) the nonstatutory double patenting was overcome by submitting the terminal disclaimer, (iii) relevant allowable matter identified in claims 2 and 3 was incorporated into claim 1, (iv) that amendments to the claims obviated the rejection under 35 U.S.C. §103, and (v) that

independent claim 19 was now allowable. In particular, arguments were presented that the control signal may be configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction and the verbal instruction may comprise the discrete steps of the course correction (emphasis added).

The Examiner, Frank T Glenn III, issued a Final Office Action on October 31, 2023 that (i) withdrew the objection to claim 7, (ii) withdrew the nonstatutory double patenting rejections, (iii) allowed claims 1, 2, 4-10 and 19, (iv) rejected claims 11-18 under 35 U.S.C. §103, and (v) notified that independent claims 1, 11 and 19 were being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. §112(f). In
particular, claim 11 was rejected over (U.S. Patent No. 10,424,204 B1), in view of Sabeti (U.S. Application No 2015/0175072 Al), and in further view of Nagy (U.S. Application No. 2020/0132803 Al).

In rejecting claim 11, the Examiner cited Han for "an auditory warning, a sound or alert performed by a horn or external speaker installed at stationary vehicle 110" and Nagy for "direct that the other vehicle activate its braking system". Activating
the braking system was presented as reading on "said discrete steps comprise instructions for a driver of said moving object" of claim
11. The analysis of the Examiner did not indicate how applying the brakes in Nagy, a singular step, read on providing discrete steps
(plural).

Applicants' representative filed a Response After Final Action on November 30, 2023 (the "After Final Response") that amended claims 1, 7, 11, and 14, canceled claim 12 and added new claims 20-22 that depend from claim 11. The After Final Response included (i) an argument regarding the interpretation under 35 U.S.C. §112(f), (ii) arguments obviating the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §103, (iii) a statement regarding a showing under 37 CFR §1.116, and (iv) a request for the After Final Consideration Pilot (AFCP) program 2.0.

The statement regarding a showing under 37 CFR §1.116 stated that claim 1 has been entered and allowed and the amendment to claim 1 and 11 is believed to resolve interpretation under 35 U.S.C. §112(f). Claims 1 and 11 were amended from a "capture device" to an "interface" to resolve the interpretation under 35 U.S.C. §112(f). At no point in the arguments obviating the rejection under 35 U.S.C. §103 was the "interface" referred to as overcoming prior art.
The statement regarding a showing under 37 CFR §1.116
stated that the "amendment to claims 7 and 14 clarify an antecedent issue". There was no prior art for claim 7 to overcome.
The statement regarding a showing under 37 CFR §1.116
stated that the "amendment to claim 11 and newly added claims 20-22 narrow the claims to better focus the claims for appeal and/or for

the concurrently submitted After Final Consideration Pilot Program request". In particular, claim 11 was amended to add the limitations "(v) determine a course correction for said moving obiect to prevent said moving object from colliding with said vehicle" and "wherein, ... (iv) said plurality of discrete steps comprise instructions for a driver of said moving object". Claim 20 regards examples of the plurality of discrete steps. Claim 21 regards determine whether the moving object performed the first of the plurality of discrete steps using said computer vision operations and re-analyzing the course correction for the moving object in response to determining that the first of the plurality of discrete steps has not been performed. Claim 22 regards

repeating the first of the plurality of discrete steps in response to the re-analysis of the course correction for the moving object if the moving object has not performed the first of the plurality of discrete steps.
The Examiner, Frank T Glenn III, issued an Advisory Action on December 14, 2023. The Advisory Action stated "3. The

proposed amendments filed after a final rejection, but prior to the date of filing a brief, will not be entered because" "a) They raise new issues that would require further consideration and/or search (see NOTE below)" and "c) They are not deemed to place the application in better form for appeal by materially reducing or simplifying the issues for appeal". The Advisory Action stated "12. The request for reconsideration has been considered but does NOT place the application in condition for allowance because: See
Continuation Sheet" and "14. Other: See Continuation Sheet".
The Continuation Sheet on The Advisory Action stated that
for (3) :

Continuation of 3. NOTE: The proposed amendments to independent claims 1 and 11 include limitations not present in a previously-examined claim set and have therefore not yet been considered by the Examiner. In particular, the scope of the claims has been modified by amending the claims to include the limitations "an interface configured to receive pixel data corresponding to an exterior view from a vehicle; "Such a modification of the scope of the claims necessitates further search and consideration, as "an interface" differs from "a capture device" and "receive" differs from "generate".

Further, new claims 20-22 include features which have not yet been examined (including but not limited to features directed towards re-analysis of course correction); as such, the amendments to the claims are not deemed to place the application in better form for appeal by materially reducing or simplifying the issues for appeal.

The Continuation Sheet on The Advisory Action for (12) indicated that the claims include limitations not present in a previously-examined claim set, and additional search and consideration would be required before a decision regarding allowability can be considered. The Continuation Sheet on The Advisory Action for (14) indicated that the AFCP 2.0 request was denied because the response cannot be reviewed and a search conducted in the limited amount of time authorized by the pilot program.
The Advisory Action did not cure the deficiencies of the Final Action. The Advisory Action did not enter the amendments to the claims as requested.
This petition requests that the following points be reviewed:
1. The Examiner improperly did not enter the amended claims from the After Final Response, despite the clear request under 37 CFR §1.116.

2. The Examiner improperly indicated that the amendments would require further consideration or search. In particular, the Examiner cited the "interface configured to receive pixel data" as a new element. However, the claimed "interface configured to receive pixel data" in claims 1 and 11 were provided regarding the claim interpretation under 35 U.S.C. §112(f), and were not related to overcoming prior art. The amendments to claim 7 and 14 only address antecedent issues. No additional search was required.
3. Regarding claim 11, the Examiner improperly filed an incomplete Office Action due to a failure to address all the words of the claim limitations as required by 37 CFR §1.104(b). In

particular, the Examiner failed to respond to the claimed "discrete steps", as claimed. The Applicant recognizes that new limitations were added, the "plurality" added to "discrete steps" were added limitations to satisfy the narrowing requirement for the AFCP 2.0 request. The claims, as originally filed, always included the plural "steps", which was never addressed by the singular "brake" instruction in Nagy. While the Applicant recognizes that claim interpretation is not suitable for a petition, the Applicant should not be penalized for adding narrowing the claim for the AFCP 2.0

request that was ignored by the Examiner, and then also be penalized because the limitation that narrows the claim involves too much additional search and consideration. In particular, as noted above, the "interface" limitation is not related to prior art. The only additional search and consideration becomes the plurality of discrete steps, which should have been addressed by the Examiner previously. Furthermore, "plurality of discrete steps" would narrow issues on appeal to avoid any potential confusion over interpreting discrete steps as a singular step.

4. Regarding claims 20-22, since there is no need for the Examiner to search and consider the claimed "interface" in claims 1 and 11, the Examiner should have more time available to review the new claim limitations in the time allotted for the pilot program

Applicants' representative respectfully presents this petition for a complete Office Action. Applicants' representative respectfully requests that (i) a new non-final Office Action is provided addressing each and every one of the limitations, as claimed, and/or (ii) the amendments provided in the After Final Response be entered. Because the Final Office Action was believed to be procedurally incomplete, no fee is required for this petition.
